topic: Matrix Multiplication as Composition of Linear Transformations

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Transformation View
sections.content: Briefly define a linear transformation as a function T(v) = Av that moves a vector in space. Visualize this as a 'grid morphing' animation where a matrix A stretches or rotates a 2D coordinate system.
sections.example: A 2D vector [1, 0] being mapped to [0, 1] by a rotation matrix.

sections.title: The Concept of Composition
sections.content: Explain that applying two transformations in sequence (T2 after T1) is equivalent to a single transformation. Define this as T(v) = T2(T1(v)). Use a 'Robot Arm' analogy where the first joint rotates and the second joint translates relative to the first.
sections.example: Robot Arm: Joint A rotates the base, Joint B rotates the forearm; the final position is a composition of both actions.

sections.title: Bridging to Matrix Multiplication
sections.content: Show mathematically that if T1(v) = Av and T2(u) = Bu, then T2(T1(v)) = B(Av) = (BA)v. Emphasize that the matrix BA represents the combined effect of A followed by B.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'Stretch' matrix (A) followed by a 'Rotate' matrix (B), resulting in a single 'Spiral' matrix (BA).

sections.title: Visualizing the 'Why': The Grid Perspective
sections.content: Use an animation showing a unit square. Step 1: Apply matrix A (shearing). Step 2: Apply matrix B to the result. Show that the final grid matches applying the single matrix product (BA) directly to the original square.
sections.example: A square being sheared by matrix A and then flipped by matrix B, showing the final state equals the product BA.

sections.title: Summary & Order Sensitivity
sections.content: Conclude by highlighting why BA does not usually equal AB. Just like putting on socks then shoes is different from shoes then socks, the order of transformations matters. Reinforce that matrix multiplication is simply the 'bookkeeping' for successive transformations.
sections.example: A 2D character sprite: Rotating then Scaling looks different than Scaling then Rotating.
